key_insight: Computation time distributions can act as observable signatures of the underlying mechanism, not just a measure of speed.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to compare and diagnose finite computational systems—classical, biological, neuromorphic, or quantum—without needing direct access to their internal architecture.
method: Benchmark computation time scaling with problem size.
Analyze full time distributions as mechanistic signatures.
Compare human visual search against models with different evidence-accumulation mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that benchmarking gave similar scaling for humans and all three models, while distributional analysis separated the models by mechanism.
watch_item: Distribution-based inference may be sensitive to noise, task design, and limited sample sizes, so mechanistic conclusions should be treated as indirect rather than definitive.
paper_title: Distributional signatures of computation: inferring mechanisms from computation time distributions
